title: Stabilization of kernels of pointed product maps from powers of a connected smooth group
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G$ be a smooth connected affine $k$-group scheme of finite type and $J$ an affine $k$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $r\geq1$ and let $\varphi:G^r\to J$ be a $k$-morphism carrying the identity tuple to $e_J$; $\varphi$ need not be a homomorphism. Powers are fibre products over $k$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For each $n\geq1$ put $w_n:G^{rn}\to J$, $w_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=\varphi(x_1)\cdots\varphi(x_n)$, where $x_i\in G^r$, and $I_n=\ker(w_n^*:k[J]\to k[G^{rn}])$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Every $G^m$, $m\geq1$, is geometrically integral [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible, def-pc-integral-scheme]. There is $N\geq1$ for which $I_n=I_N$ for all $n\geq N$, and $I_N$ is a prime ideal. Consequently $\bigcap_{n\geq1}I_n=I_N$, the affine scheme $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(k[J]/I_N)$ is integral, and $w_N$ factors through a morphism $G^{rN}\to Z$ with dense image and injective pullback on coordinate algebras.

source.place: Proposition 6.20(a), printed p.130, prime-kernel stabilization argument, generalized from the commutator map to an arbitrary pointed map G^r to J; Section 2h, printed pp.54–56, product maps; smooth connected group-variety geometry used there

proof.text: The identity section gives a point of $G$ with residue field $k$: its residue-field maps $k\to\kappa(e)\to k$ compose to the identity and the second is an injective field map, hence both are isomorphisms. Apply [lem-trf-connected-point-geometrically-connected] to this point and the assumed connectedness of $G$. Thus $G$ is geometrically connected. Apply [lem-trf-smooth-connected-fibre-normal-integrality] to $G\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. The base has just one point, its fibre is $G$, and the smoothness and nonempty geometric connectedness hypotheses hold. For every field extension $K/k$ it gives integrality of $G_K$. Consequently $G$ is geometrically integral, and in particular geometrically irreducible, by [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible, def-pc-integral-scheme].

source.place: Proposition 6.20(a), smooth connected geometry; Stacks 04KV (lemma-geometrically-connected-if-connected-and-point), 056T (lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal), and 057J (lemma-normal-morphism-irreducible)

proof.text: Induct on $m\geq1$, with base $m=1$ from Step 1, to prove that $G^m$ is affine, smooth over $k$, and geometrically irreducible. In the induction step, $G^{m+1}=G^m\times_kG$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Its projection to $G^m$ is the base change of $G\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, hence smooth by clause (2) of [lem-pc-proper-base-change]; composing with the smooth structure map of $G^m$ is smooth by [lem-trf-smooth-composition]. Apply [lem-sc-geometrically-irreducible-product] to the two factors for geometric irreducibility. Finally [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced] gives geometric reducedness of $G^m$. For every $K/k$, $(G^m)_K$ is therefore both reduced and nonempty irreducible, hence integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. This proves geometric integrality of every power, and its affine coordinate algebra $k[G^m]$ is a domain.

Write $A=k[J]$ and $B_n=k[G^{rn}]$. Iterated multiplication in $J$, composed with the copies of $\varphi$, defines $w_n$ using [def-sc-group-scheme, def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $s_n:G^{rn}\to G^{r(n+1)}$ append the identity tuple of $G^r$. The equation $\varphi(e,\ldots,e)=e_J$ and the unit law give $w_{n+1}\circ s_n=w_n$, as morphisms (equivalently on points over every $k$-algebra). By contravariant functoriality in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $w_n^*=s_n^*\circ w_{n+1}^*$, whence $I_{n+1}\subseteq I_n$. Step 2 makes each $B_n$ a nonzero domain. Thus $1\notin I_n$, and if $ab\in I_n$ then $w_n^*(a)w_n^*(b)=0$, so one factor vanishes and $a\in I_n$ or $b\in I_n$. This is precisely primality of $I_n$.

source.place: Section 2h, printed p.54, identity-appending maps and kernels; Proposition 6.20(a), prime kernels

proof.text: Apply [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] to the finite-type $k$-scheme $J$, obtaining a finite integer bound $d$ on lengths of strict chains of nonempty irreducible closed subsets, for $\kundim J$ as defined by [def-kun-dimension], which is the Krull dimension of the underlying space $|J|$ in the sense of [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. For each prime $I_n\subset A$, $V(I_n)$ is the closure of the point $I_n$ in $\operatorname{Spec}A=J$: the closed set $V(L)$ contains that point exactly when $L\subseteq I_n$, in which case it contains all primes containing $I_n$. Such a closure is nonempty irreducible: if it is covered by two closed subsets, its distinguished point lies in one, and its whole closure lies there. For primes $Q\subsetneq P$, $V(P)\subsetneq V(Q)$, since the point $Q$ belongs to $V(Q)$ but not to $V(P)$. Hence any finite strictly decreasing subsequence of the $I_n$ of length $t$ yields a strict chain of irreducible closed subsets of $J$ of length $t$, so $t\leq d$.

source.place: Proposition 6.20(a), chain termination: explicit finite-dimensional argument; Stacks Topology 0055 (definition-Krull)

proof.text: If the descending sequence were not eventually constant, then for every $a\geq1$ there would be $b>a$ with $I_b\ne I_a$, and hence $I_b\subsetneq I_a$. Starting with $a=1$ and choosing such a later index repeatedly $d+1$ times gives a strictly decreasing subsequence with $d+1$ strict inclusions, contradicting Step 4. Therefore some $N\geq1$ satisfies $I_n=I_N$ for every $n\geq N$. This argument uses only the finite bound of Step 4 and descent from Step 3; it does not assert that equality at just one adjacent pair forces stabilization. Primality of $I_N$ was proved in Step 3.

For $n<N$ descent gives $I_N\subseteq I_n$, while for $n\geq N$ equality holds. Thus $\bigcap_{n\geq1}I_n=I_N$. Set $C=A/I_N$. Since $I_N$ is proper prime, $C$ is nonzero, and $\bar a\bar b=0$ implies $ab\in I_N$, hence $\bar a=0$ or $\bar b=0$; thus $C$ is a domain. The zero prime is a generic point of $Z=\operatorname{Spec}C$ by the closed-set computation in Step 4, so $Z$ is nonempty irreducible. Every stalk $C_{\mathfrak p}$ is a domain: $C\to C_{\mathfrak p}$ is injective and a zero product of fractions has zero numerator product in $C$. Thus its stalks have no nonzero nilpotents, giving reducedness by [def-pc-reduced-scheme], and then integrality by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. The formula $\bar a\mapsto w_N^*(a)$ is well defined because $I_N=\ker(w_N^*)$, and injective by the same equality. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient] it defines $v:G^{rN}\to Z$ with $w_N=i\circ v$, where $i:Z\to J$ is induced by $A\to C$. Its pullback is exactly this injective map.

source.place: Proposition 6.20(a), quotient by the stabilized prime kernel; Section 2h, printed p.54, quotient factorization

proof.text: Let $h:C\hookrightarrow B_N$ be the pullback just constructed. The zero ideal of the domain $B_N$ is a point of $G^{rN}$; its image under $\operatorname{Spec}h$ is $h^{-1}(0)=0$ by injectivity. The closure of the zero prime in $\operatorname{Spec}C$ is $V(0)=\operatorname{Spec}C$, by the closed-set computation in Step 4. Thus the image of $v$ contains a dense point, so is dense in $Z$. This proves the last clause without any claim that $\varphi$ is a homomorphism or that its image is closed under inverses.

source.place: Section 2h, printed p.55, schematic dominance and density; direct affine generic-point proof

lean.statement: theorem pointedProductWordKernel_stabilization (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (G J : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GrpObj G] [GrpObj J] [IsAffine G.left] [IsAffine J.left] [Smooth G.hom] [ConnectedSpace G.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom] (r : ℕ) (hr : 1 ≤ r) (φ : (∏ᶜ fun _ : Fin r ↦ G) ⟶ J) (hφ : Pi.lift (fun _ : Fin r ↦ (1 : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ G)) ≫ φ = 1) : (∀ m : ℕ, 1 ≤ m → GeometricallyIntegral (∏ᶜ fun _ : Fin m ↦ G).hom) ∧ ∃ N : ℕ, 1 ≤ N ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n → pointedProductWordKernel φ n = pointedProductWordKernel φ N) ∧ (pointedProductWordKernel φ N).IsPrime ∧ (⨅ n : {n : ℕ // 1 ≤ n}, pointedProductWordKernel φ n.val) = pointedProductWordKernel φ N ∧ IsIntegral (Spec (.of (Γ(J.left, ⊤) ⧸ pointedProductWordKernel φ N))) ∧ ∃ v : (∏ᶜ fun _ : Fin N ↦ (∏ᶜ fun _ : Fin r ↦ G)).left ⟶ Spec (.of (Γ(J.left, ⊤) ⧸ pointedProductWordKernel φ N)), v ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk (pointedProductWordKernel φ N))) ≫ J.left.isoSpec.inv = (pointedProductWord φ N).left ∧ DenseRange v.base ∧ Function.Injective v.appTop
